Transaction value about $5.1B; Eaton shareholders to own at least 50.1% of the combined company, Dana shareholders about 49.9%; Eaton receives a cash distribution of approximately $1.1B; the combined company expects ~$11B pro forma revenue and ~$1.7B 2026 adjusted EBITDA including $250M run-rate synergies; closing expected in the first quarter of 2027 subject to approvals. Eaton, February 2026 (fourth-quarter release, Yahoo Finance mirror): full-year 2025 sales a record $27.4B, up 10% from 2024. Boilerplate: Eaton Corporation plc is an intelligent power management company headquartered in Dublin, listed on the NYSE as ETN.

Eaton / Business Wire, 16 March 2026: Eaton and NVIDIA unveiled the Eaton Beam Rubin DSX platform, a modular pre-engineered data-centre platform for NVIDIA NVL72 racks, with Eaton's 800 V DC infrastructure written into NVIDIA's reference designs; the collaboration spans switchgear, UPS and automation for megawatt-class racks (Data Center Frontier).

Eaton, 2 March 2026: David B. Foster appointed Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer effective 2 March 2026, succeeding Olivier Leonetti (left 13 March 2026). Senior leadership listing (search summary of the corporate-officers page): Heath Monesmith, President and Chief Operating Officer, Electrical Sector; Mike Yelton, President, Electrical Sector Americas. No chief marketing officer is listed; marketing and communications sit at director level (Camie Hanily, global marketing and communications director, per GlobalData).

GM News (19 Jan 2026) and Inside INdiana Business / Indianapolis Business Journal: the Cadillac F1 Team is owned by General Motors and TWG Motorsports (CEO Dan Towriss); its $200M, 400,000 sq ft headquarters in Fishers, Indiana is under construction and will employ about 300 people; the team also operates a power-unit facility in Concord, North Carolina, a site in Warren, Michigan, and European operations from Silverstone, England.

Formula1.com, 2026 regulations explained: the MGU-K rises from 120 kW to 350 kW so that around 50 per cent of the power unit's output is electrical (about 20 per cent under the previous rules); the ICE falls to roughly 400 kW; all cars run advanced sustainable fuel.

ABB: Formula E championship title partner since 2018. Aston Martin Aramco: Aramco title, ARM, Cognizant, NetApp, CoreWeave. Mercedes: Signify, HPE, AMD. Williams: Duracell, Komatsu. Alpine: Eni. Audi: Extreme Networks. Haas: Haas Automation.
2026 F1 calendar table: Miami GP in the first half, United States GP (Austin) in late October, Las Vegas GP in November.

brief.hq: Dublin (operations run from the United States)
brief.deck: Eaton, the $27.4B intelligent-power group, agreed on 10 June 2026 to separate its Mobility business and combine it with Dana in a ~$5.1B Reverse Morris Trust, taking about $1.1B in cash. What remains is a pure electrical and aerospace company riding a 240% surge in US data-centre orders.
brief.the_case_p1: On 10 June 2026 Eaton signed definitive agreements to separate its Mobility business and combine it with Dana in a Reverse Morris Trust valued at about $5.1B. Eaton shareholders keep at least 50.1% of the combined company, Eaton receives roughly $1.1B in cash, and closing is expected in the first quarter of 2027. The vehicle heritage leaves; intelligent power stays. First-quarter sales were a record $7.5B, up 17%, Electrical Americas reached $3.6B, up 20%, data-centre orders rose about 240% and organic growth guidance went to 10%.
brief.the_case_p2: The identity reset arrives with money and a story: 2025 sales were a record $27.4B, and in March Eaton and NVIDIA unveiled the Beam Rubin DSX platform for 800-volt AI factories. Every F1 factory, wind tunnel and garage is a power problem, and from 2026 the cars draw about half their output electrically. The electrical-equipment category on the grid is held by two European rivals, Siemens and Schneider Electric; the American incumbent is absent.
brief.why_now_callout: <font name='Poppins-Bold' size='9'>WHY NOW</font>  The Dana agreement was signed on 10 June and closes in the first quarter of 2027: the window in which Eaton decides what the remaining company stands for. Teams close 2027 rosters in Q4, and the United States GP (Austin) and Las Vegas GP sit inside it.
brief.why_team_para: Cadillac is the first American works entry in a generation: General Motors and TWG Motorsports, a $200M, 400,000 sq ft headquarters under construction in Fishers, Indiana, a power-unit facility in Concord, North Carolina, and a European base at Silverstone. Its inaugural roster is Claro, Core Scientific, IFS, Jim Beam, Tenneco, Tommy Hilfiger and TWG AI: no electrical, power or energy brand. Eaton is the US incumbent in switchgear and UPS; a new campus is specified once.
brief.value_content: MODE A - operational. Three Cadillac sites are being fitted out at once. Eaton supplies the medium-voltage switchgear, power distribution, UPS and circuit protection for Fishers, Concord and Silverstone, with data-centre-grade monitoring across dyno rooms and simulators. Trackside, Eaton power-quality and backup kit runs the garage and pit wall. In return: Official Power Management Partner, engine-cover or halo placement, Austin and Las Vegas hospitality for Eaton's utility and data-centre buyers.
brief.deal_arch_para: Entry as Official Power Management Partner. <font name='Poppins-Bold' size='9.5'>THREE YEARS</font>, 2027-2029, bridging the Dana closing and the first seasons of the pure-play Eaton. Estimated $5-8M a year, part in equipment and engineering. Scope: campus and trackside power infrastructure, engine-cover or halo branding, US-race hospitality, engineering content from the Fishers build.

why_now.label: Trigger
why_now.text: On 10 June 2026 Eaton signed definitive agreements to separate its Mobility business and combine it with Dana Incorporated in a Reverse Morris Trust. The transaction is valued at about $5.1B; Eaton shareholders will own at least 50.1% of the combined company and Eaton receives a cash distribution of about $1.1B. Closing is expected in the first quarter of 2027, subject to shareholder and regulatory approvals.

why_now.label: A company changing what it is
why_now.text: The vehicle and mobility heritage leaves with Dana. What remains is intelligent power: electrical equipment for data centres, utilities, buildings and industry, plus aerospace. A company that has just redrawn its perimeter has to tell customers, investors and recruits what it now stands for, and that is when brand budgets are re-cut.

why_now.label: Peak demand
why_now.text: First-quarter 2026 sales were a record $7.5B, up 17%; Electrical Americas reached $3.6B, up 20%, with data-centre orders up about 240% and sector backlog up 48%. In March Eaton and NVIDIA unveiled the Beam Rubin DSX platform for 800-volt AI factories. Eaton is selling into the largest capital build-out in the US economy and has raised 2026 organic growth guidance to 10%.

why_now.label: Calendar window
why_now.text: Teams close their 2027 partner rosters in the fourth quarter. The United States GP (Austin) in late October and the Las Vegas GP in November are the US stages inside that window; a deal agreed before Austin can be announced in the US and launched in full when the Dana transaction closes in Q1 2027.

why_team.label: The open lane
why_team.text: Cadillac's inaugural 2026 roster is Claro, Core Scientific, IFS, Jim Beam, Tenneco, Tommy Hilfiger and TWG AI. There is no electrical-equipment, power or energy brand. Official Power Management Partner is a clean category on a team whose commercial inventory is still being built.

why_team.label: An American works team
why_team.text: Cadillac is the only entry owned by an American manufacturer, General Motors, with TWG Motorsports. Eaton is the incumbent US name in switchgear, UPS and power distribution, Dublin-domiciled but run from the United States. The pairing reads naturally in Austin, Miami and Las Vegas, where Eaton's utility, data-centre and industrial customers sit.

why_team.label: Three sites to power
why_team.text: A $200M, 400,000 sq ft headquarters is under construction in Fishers, Indiana; a power-unit facility runs in Concord, North Carolina; European operations are led from Silverstone. New buildings are specified once. A power partner who arrives during the fit-out becomes part of the building, not a sticker on it.

why_team.label: Rivals are elsewhere
why_team.text: Siemens sits on the rosters of both Red Bull teams and Schneider Electric joined McLaren for 2026. Neither can be displaced; Cadillac is the one competitive, well-funded team where the category has never been sold.

value.label: Operational workstream (Mode A)
value.text: Medium-voltage switchgear, power distribution, uninterruptible power and circuit protection for the Fishers, Concord and Silverstone sites, with the same monitoring and energy-management layer Eaton sells to data-centre operators applied to dyno rooms, simulators and machine shops. Trackside, Eaton power-quality and backup equipment runs the garage and pit-wall systems at 24 rounds.

value.label: Commercial lift for the team
value.text: Eaton brings the buyers of the AI build-out, utilities, hyperscalers, contractors and industrial groups, to Cadillac's hospitality at the three US rounds, and a founding-partner story for a team whose inventory is still being priced.

value.label: Content and ecosystem
value.text: The build of an F1 headquarters from the switchgear up is a story Eaton can tell to every data-centre customer: engineering films from Fishers, a pit-wall power reference, and a case study that maps a race garage onto an AI factory.

value.label: What the team gives back
value.text: Official Power Management Partner designation, engine-cover or halo placement, hospitality at the United States GP, Miami GP and Las Vegas GP, driver and engineering access for Eaton's customer events.

## The trigger, re-verified

The thin desk row called this `never_entered, category_whitespace, funding_event` on 20 June with an SEC exhibit from the 2025 annual results as its source. The real trigger is the **Dana Reverse Morris Trust**: definitive agreements signed **10 June 2026**, announced 11 June (Eaton release, Dana release, Eaton 8-K exhibit 99.1). Transaction value ~$5.1B; Eaton shareholders ≥ 50.1% of the combination; ~$1.1B cash to Eaton; closing expected Q1 2027. It replaces the standalone Mobility spin-off Eaton had planned. ## Judgement calls

- **Team.** The thin row pointed at Aston Martin. Chosen instead: **Cadillac F1 Team** — the only US-manufacturer works entry, three sites in fit-out (a greenfield power specification is the MODE A workstream), and a roster with no electrical, power or energy brand. Aston Martin is ruled out transparently (campus already built and powered; technology-heavy roster under an energy title). Siemens (both Red Bull teams), Schneider Electric (McLaren, joined 2026) and ABB (FE title) rule out the rest.
- **Ruiz's 18 years at Siemens** is context, not a motorsport tie. `leadership_ties` = none found after checking Ruiz, Foster and Monesmith.
- **Score 76, not higher.** Industrial B2B brand with no consumer pull (BRAND FIT 13); no raise or listing catalyst, the closing is the only hard date (URGENCY 13). The thin row's 76 happens to hold.
- **Deal size $5–8M a year is an ESTIMATE**, labelled as such.
- **Not used:** Eaton's Q2 2026 results (30 Jul 2026) post-date the brief; the $30M US switchgear investment (single secondary source); Eaton's motorsport supply heritage (superchargers, differentials) sits in the Mobility business that is leaving, so it is not claimed as a tie.
- **Cadillac's launch-material partners** Tommy Hilfiger, Pirelli and Alpinestars are named from the team's announcement (search summary), not the sponsor table; no 'Brand at Team' sentence depends on them.
